Task: build and run `mise run release:smoke` in entire-brain — one end-to-end smoke
suite proving the full user journey on a locally complete setup. This is a stable-
release gate artifact.

Context (decisions already made, do not relitigate):
- This is a tripwire, not a test suite: one runnable script, ~7 asserts, no
  frameworks, no fixtures beyond one tiny session transcript and one tiny code repo.
- Stable release is brain v0.2.0 / graph v0.5.0; the smoke runs against the RC SHA.
- A separate workspace (COR-2233/2234/2235/2236) is changing memory-sync defaults
  (per-fact wire becomes the connected default; gitmeta default retired). Pin the
  smoke's sync legs with EXPLICIT backend flags so the suite stays valid before and
  after that work lands, and leave a comment noting it.

What the suite must prove, in order, each with one assert that fails loudly:
1. Setup: create a scratch git repo (temp dir), enable entire + brain on it,
   assert status reports healthy. Run `entire agent-help` and
   `entire agent-help <cmd>` to get exact current flags — do not guess commands.
2. Capture: make a commit with a session present and assert a checkpoint was
   captured (commits auto-capture; never create checkpoints by hand).
3. Distill: run real `entire brain distill` over ONE tiny fixture transcript
   (a few chunks, cheap model/effort if flags allow) and assert >= 1 fact
   was written. --dry-run is not sufficient; it proves planning, not extraction.
   Requires a coding agent on PATH — check and fail with a clear message if absent.
4. Recall: `entire brain recall` for the fixture fact's content, assert it comes
   back (facts are branch-scoped — query the branch you distilled on).
5. Graph query: `entire graph query --repo <scratch> --head` for a known symbol
   in the fixture code, assert it resolves.
6. Upload: connect the scratch repo to the STAGING brainstore org (document the
   env vars/credentials the runner must export; never hardcode secrets) and sync
   memories up with the explicit hosted backend flag; assert success exit + the
   fact visible remotely. Respect that ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS must be unset here.
7. Pull + merge: second scratch clone, connect, pull memories down, assert the
   fact arrives and merges into the local store.

Implementation constraints:
- One bash script under mise-tasks/ wired as `release:smoke` in the existing mise
  task convention (read mise.toml and the existing release:evidence task first and
  match their patterns, including output/evidence conventions).
- Evidence: write a timestamped summary (pass/fail per leg, versions of brain,
  graph, and host entire CLI from their version commands) to a file; redact host
  paths before anything is committed (release:evidence precedent).
- Cleanup: temp repos removed on exit, including on failure (trap).
- No new dependencies. Keep it boring.

Definition of done:
- `mise run release:smoke` passes end-to-end on this machine with a fully set-up
  environment, and you paste the evidence summary in the PR.
- Script + task land via the normal PR flow: pull latest main first, branch,
  explicit `git add` of named files, run the local `oxfmt` CI check before push.
- If a leg cannot pass because of an environment/credential gap, say so explicitly

[tasks."test:ci"]
description = "Run tests with race detection"
run = "go test -race ./..."

# The pre-push gate CONTRIBUTING.md points at. Deliberately NOT `test`:
# `test` is cached, which is right for the inner loop and wrong as the last
# thing you do before pushing -- a cached pass says a previous tree was green,
# not this one. Deliberately NOT `test:ci` either: that is -race, and
# internal/cli alone runs 17-20 minutes under -race on a developer machine
# while saturating it. CI owns -race; this owns "is the tree I am about to
# push actually green".
[tasks."test:prepush"]
description = "Uncached full suite + fmt + vet, the gate before you push"
run = """
set -e
go test ./... -count=1
# gofmt -l PRINTS the offending files and still exits 0, so running it bare
# under `set -e` is a check that can never fail. CI gets this right; a
# pre-push gate that does not is worse than none, because it sends people to
# push work CI will reject for exactly the thing the gate claimed to cover.
unformatted=$(gofmt -l -s .)
if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then
  echo "unformatted files:"
  echo "$unformatted"
  exit 1
fi
go vet ./...
"""

Find the code for a task from a plain-language query (start here)

Usage:
  entire graph query --query "issue or concept" --repo . [--top-k 10] [--format text|json|ndjson|agent] [--head] [--profile fast|full] [--deep]
  entire graph query [flags] "issue or concept"

Ranked source regions for a plain-language description, with source and file:line inline, budgeted to drop straight into context. This is the first move for almost every locate task.

By default query returns: ranked candidate fix sites (top hits as full function bodies), RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST plus other tests over the same code (ALSO COVERING), SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL (every place the concept is named, tagged EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC), a VERIFY line (the narrowest test command for the file), and a CLOSED-SET WARNING when a switch over a sealed set would fail at runtime. The three reference blocks (container map, signature types, declaration card) are OFF by default because they cost turns in agent sessions; --reference-blocks all turns them on for interactive reading.

--verify-block off (or --omit-verify, or ENTIRE_GRAPH_VERIFY_BLOCK=off) removes the VERIFY block and nothing else: the test command and the run-once/fix/stop advice that rides with it. That advice would help an agent with no tool just as much, so it exists for fair A/B comparisons (both arms get it, or neither). JSON then omits verify_command and reports stats.verify_omitted. In agent format the freed bytes go to ranked results under the same --max-context-bytes, so off is a different selection, not the on payload with lines deleted.

--top-k caps normal results, including automatic related sites and covering tests, without changing retrieval strategy. Explicit --callee-hop may add called-helper results beyond that cap, under its existing byte-budget and ranked-source protections. --deep additionally runs the exhaustive sparse (BM25) pass and fuses it with the semantic ranking (slower, reads every eligible file).

Ranking returns one region per unit, which is right for code and wrong for whole prose documents: one markdown document can hold the answer across several distant regions. So for prose the unit is the SECTION, not the file — a document's headed sections are ranked against every other section on their own scores, exactly as independent files would be (--document-resolution ranks a document as one unit instead). Separately, and on prose of any shape including headed documents, when fewer distinct units match than --top-k asked for, the spare slots are spent returning finer regions of the same document as results of their own (multi-resolution retrieval) — strictly additive, so it never displaces a unit and never breaches --max-context-bytes. --single-resolution turns that off. The two stack: a headed document can be ranked by section AND have spare slots filled with promoted passages, so a prose payload may carry both.

Flags:
  --query <text>            The task or bug in one plain sentence; alternatively supply one final argument
  --repo <path>             Repository to search (default: current repo)
  --top-k <n>               Maximum normal results, including related/covering entries (--callee-hop may add helpers) (default: 10)
  --format text|json|ndjson|agent
                            Output format; text is tiered for reading, agent is compact (default: json)
  --head                    Search the committed tree (cached) instead of the working tree
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                            Parsing depth; use full for bug-fix/locate (call-graph active) (default: fast)
  --deep                    Also run the exhaustive BM25 pass and fuse it (slower)
  --callee-hop              Add called-helper results beyond --top-k, subject to byte-budget and ranked-source protections
  --single-resolution       One result per ranked unit; do not spend spare slots on finer regions of a prose document
  --document-resolution     Rank a prose document as one unit; do not rank its sections separately
  --max-context-bytes <n>   Output byte budget; 0 = unbounded. Unset with --format agent: the smallest of 4096/8192/16384 that shows the top hit whole, else 24576 (default: 24576)
  --reference-blocks all|container-map,signature-types,type-card
                            Turn reference blocks back on (off by default)
  --verify-block on|off     off removes the VERIFY block (suggested test command plus its run/fix/stop advice) in every format; exists for fair A/B comparisons against an arm with no tool. Env: ENTIRE_GRAPH_VERIFY_BLOCK (default: on)
  --omit-verify             Shorthand for --verify-block off
  --max-indexed-files <n>   Bound cold-search parsing to N files
  --index-all-files         Widen cold-search parsing to every file
  --cache-dir <path>        Override the committed-tree cache directory
  --no-cache                Disable the committed-tree cache

setup is the one command that makes a repository's brain useful and keeps it
that way. It runs three phases:

  1. instant   build the deterministic core (semantic index, sessions, seed,
               docs, history). Blocking, seconds, spends NO agent tokens. The
               brain is queryable the moment this returns.
  2. backfill  distill past sessions into durable facts, NEWEST FIRST, detached
               in the background on a cheap model. Spends tokens; bounded by
               --backfill-budget and the persisted distill cache, and skipped
               entirely when no agent CLI is available.
  3. daemon    register the repo into a workspace and install ONE machine-wide
               watcher service (launchd on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux)
               so freshness never depends on remembering to run anything.
               ONE means one: the installed unit is identical for every repo and
               every workspace, and each workspace's interval, distill cadence,
               agent, model, effort and session cap live in a machine-level watch
               plan the running watcher re-reads. Setting up a second repo adds a
               row to that plan; it does not rewrite, restart or steal the
               watcher the first repo is relying on.

TOKEN SPEND: phases 2 and 3 call an agent. This is the first release in which
the watcher's --distill step and the session-end hook's distill actually run
(both were dead before), so setup is a real, recurring cost, bounded by five
gates: the fact phase ASKS before it spends (default no, and a run with no
terminal never spends unless --yes is passed), --backfill-budget sessions per
background pass, one gated agent run per --distill-every per repo, the
persisted distill cache (a session is never distilled twice), and the cheap
--model/--effort. Passing --no-backfill with --no-daemon spends nothing at all,
and "entire brain status" reports what the backfill has done so far and whether the
watcher is alive.

it can answer: at least one of the semantic index, the seed baseline or the
history index built. Those are the sources "entire brain query", "entire brain brief" and

that built) is reported as one line, skipped, and the remaining components, the

#!/bin/bash
#MISE description="Release smoke: full user journey on scratch repos (enable, capture, distill, recall, graph, hosted sync up/down)"
#
# A tripwire, not a test suite: one assert per leg, each fails loudly.
# Legs: 1 setup, 2 checkpoint capture, 3 distill, 4 recall, 5 graph query,
#        6 hosted upload (staging), 7 pull+merge on a second clone.
#
# The entire-brain binary under test is built from this checkout (the RC SHA);
# the host `entire` CLI and the entire-graph provider are the installed ones.
# Brain state is isolated per "machine" via ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*_DIR, like
# scripts/hosted-sync-smoke.sh; HOME and the host CLI's login stay real because
# legs 3 and 6 need the real coding agent and the real staging auth.
#
# Environment the runner must export (legs 6-7; never hardcode secrets):
#   REPO_ID       region-local repo ULID of a STAGING brainstore repo
#   API_URL       that repo's home-cell base URL, e.g. https://aws-us-west-2.api.partial.to/api/v1
#   AUTH_CONTEXT  optional saved `entire auth` login to mint the token from
#                 (e.g. us.auth.partial.to); default: the active context
#   ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN  optional prebuilt entire-brain binary (skips go build)
#
# Evidence: a timestamped pass/fail summary (with brain/graph/host versions)
# is written under .smoke-evidence/ with host paths redacted.
set -euo pipefail

repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
evidence_dir=${SMOKE_EVIDENCE_DIR:-"$repo_root/.smoke-evidence"}
stamp=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
evidence="$evidence_dir/release-smoke-$stamp.md"

REPO_ID=${REPO_ID:?export REPO_ID (staging brainstore repo ULID) -- see header}
API_URL=${API_URL:?export API_URL (staging cell base URL) -- see header}

# Hosted sync fails closed under the egress kill switch; this suite exists to
# exercise egress, so both spellings must be unset.
unset ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS ENTIRE_BRAIN_LOCAL_ONLY

command -v git >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL: git is required" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v entire >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL: the entire CLI is required" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v python3 >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL: python3 is required" >&2; exit 1; }
if ! command -v claude >/dev/null && ! command -v codex >/dev/null; then
  echo "FATAL: leg 3 (distill) needs a coding agent on PATH (claude or codex)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ -n "${AUTH_CONTEXT:-}" ]; then
  ENTIRE_TOKEN=$(entire auth token --context "$AUTH_CONTEXT")
else
  ENTIRE_TOKEN=$(entire auth token)
fi
export ENTIRE_TOKEN

work=$(mktemp -d)
smoke_branch="smoke-$stamp"
scratch="$work/a"
clone_b="$work/b"

declare -a leg_names=(
  "1 setup: enable + brain setup healthy"
  "2 capture: commit writes a checkpoint"
  "3 distill: real agent writes >=1 fact"
  "4 recall: distilled fact comes back"
  "5 graph: fixture symbol resolves"
  "6 upload: hosted sync up, fact visible remotely"
  "7 pull: second clone pulls + merges the fact"
)
declare -a leg_status=(not-run not-run not-run not-run not-run not-run not-run)
current_leg=0

versions() {
  printf -- '- host CLI: %s\n' "$(entire version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
  printf -- '- entire-brain (under test): %s\n' "$("$brain_bin" version 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
  printf -- '- entire-graph: %s\n' "$(entire graph version --json 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
}

finalize() {
  status=$?
  trap - EXIT
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || [ "$current_leg" -eq 0 ] || leg_status[current_leg - 1]=FAIL
  mkdir -p "$evidence_dir"
  {
    echo "# release:smoke $stamp"
    echo
    echo "result: $([ "$status" -eq 0 ] && echo PASS || echo "FAIL (exit $status)")"
    echo "rc sha: $(git -C "$repo_root" rev-parse HEAD)"
    echo "staging repo: $REPO_ID @ $API_URL"
    echo
    versions
    echo
    for i in "${!leg_names[@]}"; do
      echo "- [${leg_status[$i]}] ${leg_names[$i]}"
    done
  } | sed -e "s|$work|\$WORK|g" -e "s|$HOME|~|g" >"$evidence"
  echo
  echo "evidence: $evidence"
  cat "$evidence"
  rm -rf "$work"
  exit "$status"
}
trap finalize EXIT

leg() {
  current_leg=$1
  printf '\n== leg %s: %s\n' "$1" "${leg_names[$1 - 1]#* }"
}
pass() { leg_status[current_leg - 1]=PASS; }
fail() {
  echo "SMOKE FAIL (leg $current_leg): $1" >&2
  exit 1
}

# machine <a|b> <workdir> <cmd...>: run a command against one isolated
# "machine" (its own plugin data/state/config/cache), real HOME and login.
# GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 makes the commit hooks auto-link instead of prompting.
machine() {
  local m=$1 dir=$2
  shift 2
  (cd "$dir" && env \
    ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR="$work/$m/data" \
    ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR="$work/$m/state" \
    ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR="$work/$m/config" \
    ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR="$work/$m/cache" \
    ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_NO_REGISTER=1 \
    GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 \
    PAGER=cat GIT_PAGER=cat \
    "$@")
}

brain_a() { machine a "$scratch" env ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT="$scratch" "$brain_bin" "$@"; }
brain_b() { machine b "$clone_b" env ENTIRE_REPO_ROOT="$clone_b" "$brain_bin" "$@"; }

json_has_fact() { # json_has_fact <needle>: stdin JSON contains <needle> in any string value
  python3 -c '
import json, sys
needle = sys.argv[1]
def walk(v):
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return needle in v
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return any(walk(x) for x in v.values())
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return any(walk(x) for x in v)
    return False
sys.exit(0 if walk(json.load(sys.stdin)) else 1)' "$1"
}

echo "== build entire-brain from this checkout"
brain_bin=${ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN:-}
if [ -n "$brain_bin" ]; then
  [ -x "$brain_bin" ] || { echo "FATAL: ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN=$brain_bin is not executable" >&2; exit 1; }
else
  command -v go >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL: go is required to build entire-brain (or set ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN)" >&2; exit 1; }
  brain_bin="$work/entire-brain"
  (cd "$repo_root" && go build -o "$brain_bin" ./cmd/entire-brain)
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- leg 1: setup
leg 1

# The remote must be github-shaped or entire-brain and entire-graph derive
# different repo keys (see scripts/demo-agent-session.sh). Never fetched.
git init -q -b main "$scratch"
git -C "$scratch" config user.name 'Release Smoke'
git -C "$scratch" config user.email 'release-smoke@example.invalid'
git -C "$scratch" config commit.gpgsign false
git -C "$scratch" remote add origin "https://github.com/entireio/release-smoke-$stamp.git"

mkdir -p "$scratch/greet"
cat >"$scratch/go.mod" <<'GOMOD'
module example.com/smoke

go 1.22
GOMOD
cat >"$scratch/greet/greet.go" <<'SRC'
// Package greet formats greetings.
package greet

// Greet returns a greeting for name.
func Greet(name string) string {
	return "hello " + name
}
SRC
git -C "$scratch" add -A
git -C "$scratch" commit -qm 'feat: greeting package'
git -C "$scratch" checkout -qb "$smoke_branch"

machine a "$scratch" entire enable --agent claude-code
machine a "$scratch" sh -c "git add .entire .claude && git commit -qm 'chore: enable Entire'"
brain_a setup --no-backfill --no-daemon .
brain_a status --json --fail-on degraded >/dev/null ||
  fail "entire brain status reports a degraded brain right after setup"
pass

# -------------------------------------------------------------- leg 2: capture
leg 2

session_id=$(python3 -c 'import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4())')
transcript="$work/$session_id.jsonl"
hook() { # hook <verb> <payload-json>
  printf '%s' "$2" | machine a "$scratch" entire hooks claude-code "$1"
}

# The fixture session: a real transcript in Claude Code's shape, with the model
# substituted by this script. Hooks, session state machine and checkpoint
# writer are the real ones.
cat >"$transcript" <<JSONL
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"Greet(\"\") returns \"hello \" with a dangling space. Make an empty name greet \"there\" instead."},"timestamp":"2026-10-22T10:00:00.000Z"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"smoke-substituted-model","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I'll guard the empty name inside Greet itself rather than at the call sites, so no caller has to repeat the check."}]},"timestamp":"2026-10-22T10:00:05.000Z"}
JSONL

hook session-start "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"model\":\"smoke-substituted-model\",\"cwd\":\"$scratch\"}"
hook user-prompt-submit "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"prompt\":\"Make an empty name greet \\\"there\\\".\"}"

cat >"$scratch/greet/greet.go" <<'SRC'
// Package greet formats greetings.
package greet

// Greet returns a greeting for name. An empty name greets "there" rather than
// producing a dangling "hello ", so no caller has to check first.
func Greet(name string) string {
	if name == "" {
		return "hello there"
	}
	return "hello " + name
}
SRC
cat >>"$transcript" <<JSONL
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"smoke-substituted-model","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"tu_1","name":"Edit","input":{"file_path":"$scratch/greet/greet.go","old_string":"return \"hello \" + name","new_string":"if name == \"\" {\n\t\treturn \"hello there\"\n\t}\n\treturn \"hello \" + name"}}]},"timestamp":"2026-10-22T10:00:10.000Z"}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"tu_1","content":"The file has been updated."}]},"timestamp":"2026-10-22T10:00:11.000Z"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"smoke-substituted-model","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Done. The empty-name guard lives inside Greet rather than at each call site, so callers never see a dangling \"hello \"."}]},"timestamp":"2026-10-22T10:00:12.000Z"}
JSONL
hook stop "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"model\":\"smoke-substituted-model\"}"

# Commits auto-capture: the post-commit hook entire enable installed writes the
# checkpoint. Never create checkpoints by hand.
machine a "$scratch" sh -c "git add -A && git commit -qm 'fix(greet): greet \"there\" for an empty name'"
hook session-end "{\"session_id\":\"$session_id\",\"transcript_path\":\"$transcript\",\"model\":\"smoke-substituted-model\",\"reason\":\"clear\"}"

[ -n "$(git -C "$scratch" for-each-ref 'refs/entire/checkpoints/' 'refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/')" ] ||
  fail "the commit produced no checkpoint ref"
pass

# -------------------------------------------------------------- leg 3: distill
leg 3

brain_a refresh sessions
# Real extraction over the fixture session; --dry-run would only prove
# planning. Cheap effort keeps the spend at one tiny chunk.
distill_out=$(brain_a distill --branch "$smoke_branch" --effort low --json .)
echo "$distill_out" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
r = json.load(sys.stdin)
n = r.get("facts_written", r.get("memories_written", r.get("facts", 0)))
if isinstance(n, list):
    n = len(n)
sys.exit(0 if n and int(n) >= 1 else 1)' ||
  { echo "$distill_out" >&2; fail "distill wrote no facts from the fixture session"; }
pass

# --------------------------------------------------------------- leg 4: recall
leg 4

recall_out=$(brain_a recall "empty name greeting guard" --branch "$smoke_branch" --json)
fact_text=$(echo "$recall_out" | python3 -c '
import json, sys
facts = json.load(sys.stdin).get("facts") or []
if not facts:
    sys.exit(1)
print(facts[0].get("text") or facts[0].get("content") or "")')
[ -n "$fact_text" ] || { echo "$recall_out" >&2; fail "recall returned no facts on branch $smoke_branch"; }
pass

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- leg 5: graph
leg 5

# --head: the fixture code is committed, and the committed-tree path is the
# cached one agents use by default.
graph_out=$(machine a "$scratch" entire graph query --repo "$scratch" --head --profile full --format json --query "Greet returns a greeting for a name")
echo "$graph_out" | grep -q 'greet\.go' ||
  { echo "$graph_out" | head -c 2000 >&2; fail "graph query did not resolve the Greet fixture symbol"; }
pass

# --------------------------------------------------------------- leg 6: upload
leg 6

brain_a connect --repo-id "$REPO_ID" --api-url "$API_URL"
# COR-2233/2234/2235/2236 change the connected-repo sync default (per-fact wire
# in, gitmeta default out). The backend stays EXPLICIT here so this suite is
# valid before and after that lands; revisit the flag value when it does.
brain_a memories sync --memories-backend http --branch "$smoke_branch" --json >/dev/null ||
  fail "hosted memories sync (up) failed"

# Remote visibility, straight from the hosted store (endpoint per
# internal/factsync: GET {base}/api/v1/repos/{id}/brain/facts?branch=).
base_url=${API_URL%/api/v1}
needle=$(printf '%s' "$fact_text" | cut -c1-60)
curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ENTIRE_TOKEN" \
  "$base_url/api/v1/repos/$REPO_ID/brain/facts?branch=$smoke_branch" |
  json_has_fact "$needle" ||
  fail "the distilled fact is not visible in the hosted store"
pass

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- leg 7: pull
leg 7

git clone -q "$scratch" "$clone_b"
git -C "$clone_b" checkout -q "$smoke_branch"
brain_b connect --repo-id "$REPO_ID" --api-url "$API_URL"
# Same explicit backend pin as the upload leg (COR-2233 family).
brain_b memories sync --memories-backend http --branch "$smoke_branch" --json >/dev/null ||
  fail "hosted memories sync (down) failed"
brain_b recall "empty name greeting guard" --branch "$smoke_branch" --json |
  json_has_fact "$needle" ||
  fail "the fact pulled on machine B did not merge into its local store"
pass

echo
echo "release:smoke: all 7 legs passed"

# endpoint when the per-fact protocol replaced it (404 today). When the
# COR-2233 family exposes an explicit per-fact backend flag on `memories
# sync`, move these two legs onto that flag.
brain_a connect --repo-id "$REPO_ID" --api-url "$API_URL" ||
  fail "connect (hosted sync up) failed"

# Remote visibility, straight from the hosted store, on this run's unique
# branch (per-fact feed endpoint per internal/factsync/perfact.go:
# GET {base}/api/v1/repos/{id}/brain/facts, paginated).
needle=$(printf '%s' "$fact_text" | cut -c1-60)
remote_has_fact() { # remote_has_fact <branch> <needle>
  python3 - "$API_URL" "$REPO_ID" "$1" "$2" <<'PY'
import json, os, sys, urllib.parse, urllib.request
api, repo, branch, needle = sys.argv[1:5]
token = os.environ["ENTIRE_TOKEN"]
page = ""
for _ in range(100):
    q = {"pageSize": "500"}
    if page:
        q["pageToken"] = page
    url = f"{api}/repos/{repo}/brain/facts?{urllib.parse.urlencode(q)}"
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
    body = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))
    for item in body.get("items") or []:
        rec = item.get("record") or {}
        if rec.get("branch") == branch and needle in (rec.get("text") or ""):
            sys.exit(0)
    page = body.get("nextPageToken") or ""
    if not page:
        break
sys.exit(1)
PY
}
